translation_en:
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Hashim ibn al-Qasim narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Abu Amir al-Aqadi informed us. Both chains report it from Ikrimah ibn Ammar. [Another chain:] Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated to us (this is his wording): Abu Ali al-Hanafi, Ubaydullah ibn Abd al-Majid, informed us: Ikrimah (Ibn Ammar) narrated to us: Iyas ibn Salamah narrated to me that his father said:
We arrived at al-Hudaybiyyah with the Messenger of Allah, and we were fourteen hundred men. We had fifty sheep, which were not enough to water us all. The Messenger of Allah sat beside the well's stone rim. He either supplicated or spat into it, and it surged up, so we watered our animals and drank. Then the Messenger of Allah called us to pledge allegiance beneath the tree. I was the first person to pledge to him. The people kept pledging, until he was among them and said: Pledge allegiance, Salamah. I said: Messenger of Allah, I pledged to you at the beginning, among the first people. He said: Again. The Messenger of Allah saw that I was unarmed, meaning I had no weapon. He gave me a small shield, or a leather shield. He continued taking pledges until he was among the last people, then said: Will you not pledge allegiance to me, Salamah? I said: Messenger of Allah, I pledged to you at the beginning and in the middle of the people. He said: Again. So I pledged to him a third time. Then he said to me: Salamah, where is the small shield, or leather shield, that I gave you? I said: Messenger of Allah, my uncle Amir met me unarmed, so I gave it to him. The Messenger of Allah laughed and said: You are like the person of old who said, 'O Allah, grant me a beloved who is dearer to me than myself.'
Then the polytheists sent us proposals for a truce, and people went back and forth between us until we made peace. I was a servant to Talhah ibn Ubaydullah: I watered his horse, rubbed it down, served him, and ate from his food. I had left my family and property, migrating to Allah and His Messenger. When we made peace with the people of Makkah and mixed with one another, I came to a tree, cleared its thorns, and lay at its base. Four polytheists from Makkah came to me and began speaking ill of the Messenger of Allah. I detested them, so I moved to another tree. They hung up their weapons and lay down. While they were like that, someone called from the bottom of the valley: O Emigrants, Ibn Zunaym has been killed! I drew my sword and charged those four while they were asleep. I took their weapons and gathered them in my hand. Then I said: By the One who honored Muhammad's face, none of you will raise his head without me striking the eyes in it. I brought them, driving them before me, to the Messenger of Allah.
My uncle Amir came with a man from the Abalat clan called Mikraz, leading him to the Messenger of Allah on a horse covered with armor, along with seventy polytheists. The Messenger of Allah looked at them and said: Let them go, so they may be the first and the last to commit wrongdoing. The Messenger of Allah pardoned them, and Allah revealed the whole verse: 'He is the One who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them in the valley of Makkah, after He had given you victory over them.' (Quran 48:24)
Then we set out, returning to Madinah. We stopped at a place with a mountain between us and Banu Lihyan, who were polytheists. The Messenger of Allah prayed for whoever climbed that mountain that night to keep watch for the Prophet and his Companions. Salamah said: I climbed it that night two or three times.
Then we arrived in Madinah. The Messenger of Allah sent his camels out to pasture with Rabah, the Messenger of Allah's servant, and I went with him. I took Talhah's horse out with him to let it graze alongside the camels. At dawn, we found that Abd al-Rahman al-Fazari had raided the Messenger of Allah's grazing herd, driven all of it away, and killed its herdsman. I said to Rabah: Take this horse to Talhah ibn Ubaydullah and tell the Messenger of Allah that the polytheists have raided his herd. I stood on a hill, turned toward Madinah, and cried out three times: To the attack at dawn! Then I followed the raiders, shooting arrows at them and reciting battle verses: I am the son of al-Akwa, and today is the day of the suckling babes. I caught up with one of them and shot an arrow into his saddle until its point reached his shoulder. I said: Take that! I am the son of al-Akwa, and today is the day of the suckling babes.
By Allah, I kept shooting at them and disabling their mounts. Whenever a horseman came back toward me, I went to a tree and sat at its base, then shot him and disabled his mount. When the mountain pass narrowed and they entered its constriction, I climbed the mountain and began rolling stones down on them. I continued following them until every camel from the Messenger of Allah's herd that Allah had made available was left behind me. They left me with the camels and went on. Then I followed them, shooting at them, until they dropped more than thirty cloaks and thirty spears to lighten their load. Whenever they dropped anything, I marked the place with piles of stones that the Messenger of Allah and his Companions would recognize.
They reached a narrow mountain pass, where a man from the Fazara tribe, so-and-so ibn Badr, joined them. They sat down to eat lunch. I sat on a mountain ridge above them. The Fazari asked: What is this I see? They said: By Allah, we have suffered greatly from this man. He has not left us since the early dawn; he has kept shooting at us until he took everything in our hands. He said: Let four of you go up to him. Four of them climbed the mountain to me. When they came close enough to speak, I said: Do you know me? They said: No. Who are you? I said: I am Salamah ibn al-Akwa. By the One who honored Muhammad's face, I will catch any man among you whom I pursue, and none of you who pursues me will catch me. One of them said: I think so. They went back, and I stayed where I was until I saw the Messenger of Allah's cavalry weaving through the trees. The first was al-Akhram al-Asadi, followed by Abu Qatadah al-Ansari, followed by al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi.
I took hold of al-Akhram's reins. The raiders turned and fled. I said: Akhram, beware lest they cut you off before the Messenger of Allah and his Companions catch up. He said: Salamah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day and know that Paradise is true and the Fire is true, do not come between me and martyrdom. So I let him go. He met Abd al-Rahman. Abd al-Rahman hamstrung his horse, and al-Akhram stabbed Abd al-Rahman and killed him, then mounted his horse. Abu Qatadah, the Messenger of Allah's horseman, caught up with Abd al-Rahman, stabbed him, and killed him.
By the One who honored Muhammad's face, I kept running after them on foot until I could see nothing behind me of Muhammad's Companions or their dust. Before sunset, they turned toward a ravine with water called Dhu Qarad, intending to drink because they were thirsty. They saw me running behind them, and I drove them away from the water, so not one drop reached their lips. They went out and hurried through a mountain pass. I ran after them, caught one of them, and shot him with an arrow in the back of his shoulder. I said: Take that! I am the son of al-Akwa, and today is the day of the suckling babes. He said: May his mother lose him! Is it al-Akwa who will get us tomorrow? I said: Yes, enemy of yourself, I am al-Akwa who will get you tomorrow.
They left two horses at a mountain pass. I brought them, leading them to the Messenger of Allah. Amir caught up with me carrying a small leather flask with a little milk mixed with water and another flask of water. I performed ablution and drank. Then I came to the Messenger of Allah, who was at the water from which I had driven them away. The Messenger of Allah had taken possession of those camels, everything I had recovered from the polytheists, every spear and cloak. Bilal had slaughtered one of the camels I had recovered and was roasting some of its liver and hump for the Messenger of Allah.
I said: Messenger of Allah, let me choose one hundred men from the people and pursue the raiders, so that not one of them who can report back will remain alive. The Messenger of Allah laughed until his back teeth showed in the firelight, then said: Salamah, do you really think you could do that? I said: Yes, by the One who honored you. He said: They are now being given hospitality in the land of Ghatafan. A man from Ghatafan came and said: So-and-so slaughtered a camel for them. When they uncovered its skin, they saw a cloud of dust and said: The people have come after you! So they fled.
In the morning, the Messenger of Allah said: Today, the best of our horsemen was Abu Qatadah, and the best of our foot soldiers was Salamah. Then the Messenger of Allah gave me two shares, a horseman's share and a foot soldier's share, and combined them both for me. The Messenger of Allah seated me behind him on al-Adba, and we returned to Madinah.
As we traveled, a man from the Ansar who could not be outpaced in a sprint kept saying: Is there anyone who will race me to Madinah? Is there anyone who will race me? He kept repeating it. When I heard him, I said: Do you not honor a noble person or respect a distinguished man? He said: No, unless it is the Messenger of Allah. I said: Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, let me race the man. He said: If you wish. I said: Go on ahead. I bent my legs, sprang forward, and ran. I held back for a rise or two to conserve my breath, then ran after him and held back for another rise or two. Then I pushed myself until I caught him and struck him between the shoulders. I said: By Allah, you have been beaten. He said: I think so. I beat him to Madinah.
By Allah, we stayed only three nights before we set out with the Messenger of Allah for Khaybar. My uncle Amir began reciting verses to urge the people on: By Allah, were it not for Allah, we would not have been guided, given charity, or prayed; we could never do without Your bounty. Make our feet firm when we meet the enemy, and send tranquility down upon us. The Messenger of Allah asked: Who is that? He said: I am Amir. The Messenger of Allah said: May your Lord forgive you. Whenever the Messenger of Allah specifically prayed for forgiveness for someone, that person was martyred. Umar ibn al-Khattab called out while riding his camel: Prophet of Allah, if only you had let us benefit from Amir longer!
When we reached Khaybar, their king Marhab came out swaggering with his sword, saying: Khaybar knows that I am Marhab, fully armed, a tested hero, when wars blaze as they approach. My uncle Amir came forward to meet him and said: Khaybar knows that I am Amir, fully armed, a daring hero. They exchanged two blows. Marhab's sword struck Amir's shield. Amir tried to strike Marhab low, but his sword turned back toward him and severed his main vein, and that wound caused his death.
Salamah said: I went out and found some of the Prophet's Companions saying: Amir's deeds are nullified; he killed himself. I came to the Prophet weeping and said: Messenger of Allah, Amir's deeds are nullified. The Messenger of Allah asked: Who said that? I said: Some of your Companions. He said: Whoever said that has lied. Rather, he has a double reward.
Then he sent me to Ali, whose eyes were inflamed, and said: I will give the standard to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, or whom Allah and His Messenger love. I went to Ali and brought him, leading him because his eyes were inflamed, until I brought him to the Messenger of Allah. The Messenger of Allah spat into his eyes, and he was healed. He gave him the standard. Marhab came out and said: Khaybar knows that I am Marhab, fully armed, a tested hero, when wars blaze as they approach. Ali said: I am the one my mother named Haydar, like a lion of the thickets, fearsome to behold; I will repay them with a mighty measure. He struck Marhab on the head and killed him, and then victory came through Ali.
